Installation

Warning

Currently, mofography works only with numpy == 1.23.*. We are working on making it compatible with the latest versions of numpy.

Install dependencies, Add path and Use. ⏩

You can simply try out mofography after installing just the dependencies. In fact, I would recommend this approach, since mofography is still in active development

Caution

MOFography has been tested with Python 3.9, it should work with other version of python, but, if you do encounter any issues, please let us know by opening an issue. Hence, feel free to create a new Python 3.9 environment for this package like this before using

conda create -n mgr_env python=3.9
conda activate mgr_env
  • Install the dependencies using conda or pip. You may create a new conda environment with python 3.9 for this, but it is not necessary.

Install Dependencies using Conda

Note

Note: In all the steps below, feel free to replace conda with mamba, as it is much faster at resolving dependencies and installing packages. To install mamba use conda install -c conda-forge -n base mamba

conda create -n mgr_env python=3.9
conda activate mgr_env
conda install -c conda-forge pymatgen ase dask dask-jobqueue networkx scikit-image tqdm aiohttp icecream sparse scikit-learn rich trimesh pyvista plotly furl requests freud cupy

Install Dependencies using Pip

if you’d like to install these dependencies using pip, the name of the freud package is freud-analysis so use this command instead

pip install pymatgen ase dask dask-jobqueue networkx scikit-image tqdm aiohttp icecream sparse scikit-learn rich trimesh pyvista plotly furl requests freud-analysis cupy
Note

Note: If you are using a GPU, you can install the cupy package, which is a GPU-accelerated version of numpy. This will speed up the calculations significantly. If you don’t have a GPU, you can exclude cupy from the list of dependencies.j

Clone the repo 🎎

  • Clone the repo Click on the green Code button and download the zip file. Unzip the file to get the repo folder, the path to which we can add and use. Alternatively, if you are using git, you may instead clone the repo using the following command from your terminal with git installed
git clone https://github.com/arung-northwestern/mofography.git .

Update if need be 🔄

  • If you already have a cloned repo, pull the latest changes, since the package is being updated frequently
cd mofography
git pull

Add path 🔗

  • Add the path to mofography to your python path in your scripts and notebooks before you import,
import sys
import os
sys.path.append(os.path.abspath('path_to_mofography'))

of course, replace path_to_mofography with the relative path to the mofography directory on your local machine. This way we are not installing anything yet, so if there are changes to the source code, you can simply pull the latest changes using git pull and use them withouth having to reinstall the package everytime. ### Test the installation 🧪 - Import mofography to see if it works. There are CIF files in themofography/examples/TestCIFs` folder, which you can use to test the package. Let’s use a full-on clustering workflow with default parameters on the IRMOF-1 structure. More information on the inner workings of the workflow are provided in the Quick cluster tutorial.

import mofography as mgr
from ase.io import read
mat_atoms = read('path_to_mofography/examples/TestCIFs/P1-IRMOF-1.cif')
figures = mgr.quick_cluster(mat_atoms)
